name: Reused SelectionArea geometry signature buffer

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: headed WASM/WebGPU SelectionArea fixture at DPR 1 and DPR 2
hypothesisMarkdown:
## Reused SelectionArea geometry signature buffer

Retain an area-owned scratch buffer for the next geometry signature so unchanged frames compare revisions without allocating a new participant-sized signature vector. Keep the existing bounds index and geometry semantics unchanged.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement plan

Measure the same headed WASM/WebGPU SelectionArea fixture at DPR 1 and DPR 2 using the existing completed baseline, then run 35 post-change repetitions per project with five warmups discarded. Reject any p95 regression above five percent or visual/fixture failure.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected outcome

Unchanged SelectionArea frames reuse their geometry-comparison capacity rather than allocating a signature vector, while geometry revision detection and bounds behavior remain identical.

measurements.target: headed WASM/WebGPU SelectionArea fixture; 35 repetitions per DPR with five warmups discarded

reportMarkdown:
## Reused SelectionArea geometry signature buffer

Rejected and reverted. The candidate reused an area-owned scratch vector while calculating the next geometry signature. The focused DPR 1/DPR 2 fixture and the 70 repeated post-change runs passed, but DPR 1 p95 input-to-published-frame duration regressed from 95.91 ms to 104.31 ms (8.8%), exceeding the experiment's five-percent gate.

The candidate source has been restored to the checkpoint before this result is recorded. The retained direct stable-order fast path remains the accepted dormant-frame allocation reduction.
